Corporate financing is a decisive factor for the success of a company, regardless of whether it is a young start-up or an established company. Solid financing is the basis for implementing future-oriented business goals and realising targeted growth plans. We understand that every company is unique and therefore requires customised solutions.

Venture capital investments are generally divided into several financing rounds, in which various co-investors usually contribute equity to the company as part of a capital increase in return for the subscription of new shares. The target companies of a venture capital investment are young and innovative companies in the start-up or growth phase.

The participation of a private equity company often takes place as part of a single transaction in which existing shares of a selling shareholder are acquired by the private equity investor. In contrast to venture capital investments, private equity investments start later and require stable cash flows.

In the first step, our experts at EurA Ventures GmbH will support you in your search for a suitable investor from our exclusive investor network as well as in finding the right investment opportunity for you. Afterwards, we support you throughout the entire transaction process right up to closing. For us, long-term, trusting and successful cooperation is important and we ensure that your individual transaction process is structured and implemented in line with your objectives.

Samudra Oceans Limited, based in London, is pioneering the advancement of seaweed farming through cutting-edge robotics and AI technology. Named after the Sanskrit word for ‘Ocean’, Samudra is dedicated to scaling up seaweed cultivation globally in an economically viable and sustainable manner.

Our Activities:

Robotics and AI Innovation

Samudra develops modular robots designed to automate critical tasks in seaweed farming. Our current focus includes:

	•	NIRA: A compact monitoring robot that autonomously collects data on seaweed growth and environmental conditions. This includes monitoring water quality parameters like temperature and salinity, essential for optimising farm productivity.
	•	NAYAN: An AI-powered camera module that captures underwater images and videos. It analyses data to predict optimal harvest times, detect early signs of pathogens, and monitor seaweed health.

Smart Farm Technology

We integrate these technologies into ‘smart’ seaweed farms capable of minimal human intervention throughout the growth cycle. Our digital platform analyses data from our robots, providing farmers with actionable insights and predictions. This supports informed decision-making and maximises yield while minimising environmental impact.

Off-Aquaculture Farm Services

Beyond seaweed farms, Samudra offers specialised off-aquaculture farm surveys using our NIRA robots. These surveys include comprehensive data collection on environmental parameters and ecosystem health. We tailor our services to meet specific client needs, promoting sustainable practices and regulatory compliance.

Our Commitment

At Samudra Oceans Limited, we are committed to advancing sustainable marine agriculture. By harnessing robotics, AI, and data-driven insights, we aim to transform seaweed farming into a scalable solution for global food security and climate resilience.

Join us on our journey to harness the power of the ocean sustainably, for a brighter and more resilient future.

The company is also involved in molecular decontamination in the space field, and in the laser field to avoid Laser-Induced Contamination (LIC). Main results include the supply of zeolite pellets for the Curiosity and Perseverance rovers, which are exploring the planet Mars since 2011 and 2022, respectively.

ZA is developing close relationships with academic research institutions and with organisations such as the french space agency (CNES) and the french army (DGA). Recently, in collaboration with CNES, zeolite paintings with high zeolite content have been elaborated for molecular decontamination.

In 2025/26 60,000 corporations in the EU will have to disclose how their direct operations and supply chains are impacting biodiversity, for the very first time. Failure to comply can lead to fines equating to 5% of total revenue.
 
For large agricultural corporations, the regulation requires gathering biodiversity data on over 10,000 suppliers (typically farms) across 30 countries.
 
Using a combination of SAR, Multispectral and Hyperspectral imagery Biota can determine the ecosystem condition and health of priority supplier sites. This is achieved by assessing metrics such as plant photogenic activity, senescene content, and moisture readings for trees, hedges, crops and even certain plants.
 
Biota’s data analysis is provided through a SAAS model, sold directly to EU headquartered agricultural corporations.

The wearable is attached behind a user’s ear and detects any impacts that they may receive. This allows all head impacts to be detected that may have been missed by coaches or parents. It allows for quicker player recovery from concussion by ensuring that they are removed from play early. The wearable is both sports and player agnostic meaning that it can be used for any sport and by any player. User impact data is also recorded including the number and severity of impacts that a player has experienced over their playing career. The wearable uses GNSS data to determine a players speed at the time of impact.
